summary: Christopher Minkowski is an Indology scholar who studied at Harvard and Delhi, completing studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Brown, Iowa, and Cornell, and served as Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit (2005–2023).

Christopher Morris worked in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He held lecturer posts at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Literature and Science, was Professor of English Literature at Keio University (1938), and served as BBC controller (1943–1958).

Christopher Pinney is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He has held academic posts at UCL as professor of anthropology and visual culture, Northwestern University as Crowe Visiting Professor, the University of Chicago, ANU, Cape Town, and JNU.

Christopher S. George is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia under Royal W. Weiler, Geshe Wangyal, and Pema Gyaltsen, founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies, and was professor at IASWR (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. From circa 1989 to 2018, he served at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education and as a lecturer on the Study of Religion and Buddhism.

Christopher V. Jones is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He held posts at the University of Oxford, served as lecturer and research associate at Cambridge (2019–2023), and became an assistant professor at the University of Vienna in 2023.

Christopher Wallis is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Rochester, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt. In 2020, he was a guest lecturer at Naropa University.

Christophorus Becker was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He founded the Missionsärztliches Institut Würzburg in 1923, teaching there from circa 1922 to 1937, and became PD für Missionswissenschaft at the University of Würzburg in 1925.

Chu-tsing Li was a scholar of sinology and art history who studied at the University of Nanking and the University of Iowa. He taught English at Nanking, was an art history professor at Iowa (c. 1955–1966), and joined Kansas in 1966.
Chuichi Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic posts at Minobusan University, where he is attested as an associate professor in 2015 and later as a former professor in 2026.

Chulthim Gurung is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UBC and McGill. He worked at the Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and Society, and served as a teaching assistant at UBC and McGill.

Chun-i Tang was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at National Central University under Shili Xiong and Thomé H. Fang. He taught at NCU, co-founded New Asia College, and was founding chair professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Chun-min Yen is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Arizona, studying under Robert M. Gimello and Todd Brown, as well as traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.
Chung-pui Tai is a scholar of linguistics, sinology, and Tibetology who studied at the Graduate School of Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and held a post at the University of Hong Kong.

Chögyam Trungpa was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under Khenpo Gangshar and at Oxford. He served at the Young Lamas Home School and founded Kagyu Samye Ling, Naropa University, and Shambhala International.
Chökyi Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Khakyab Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, the latter of whom he also taught.
Chökyi Nyima was a scholar who pursued studies under Dudjom Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rumtek under the 16th Karmapa and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976 and founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981.
Chökyi Nyinche studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Chönyi Drolma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Thinley Norbu Rinpoche, Lama Tharchin Rinpoche, and Ngawang Zangpo (attested 2011).
